newsitem.title: UK: De La Rue sees banknote prices stabilising.
newsitem.headline: De La Rue sees banknote prices stabilising.

text.p: British printing and security products group De La Rue Plc, posting sharply lower interim results, said on Tuesday it saw signs of stabilisation in banknote pricing.
The company posted pretax profits of 60.3 million stg, down from 69.1 million a year ago, but at the top end of analysts' estimates, which ranged from 55 to 61 million stg.
De La Rue also raised its dividend to 7.5p per share compared to 7.25 in the year-ago period.
"The fact that we've put up the dividend is an indication that we're confident in the fundamentals of the business," chief executive Jeremy Marshall told Reuters in an interview.
He added that banknote prices appeared to have stabilised further since June, when the firm reported results and warned that its first-half profits would be lower than last year.
"We do have clear signs that the average prices we are obtaining are stabilising," he said.
"Up until June, we did see some deterioration in margins because prices were going up, mainly because we're putting additional security features into notes," Marshall added.
Banknote volumes increased by 14.5 percent in the first half ended September 30, compared to the year-ago period.
"We are meeting competition on the banknote side. But the group on the whole is making margins of 12 percent," he said.
De La Rue's shares shot up more than three percent by 0830, rising 19.5p to 574.5p to rank as one of the top percentage gainers on the London Stock Exchange.
